stem: A pharmacist applying to renew a Massachusetts registration discloses an out-of-state disciplinary sanction imposed solely for dispensing medication for gender-affirming health care services. The services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and consistent with good professional practice here. How should the renewal be treated?

choices.text: Renewal must be denied because any out-of-state discipline is disqualifying.
Renewal may be granted only after the other state vacates its sanction.
Renewal must be deferred pending a Massachusetts investigation of the same conduct.
Renewal may not be denied on the basis of that sanction.
Renewal may be granted only with a probationary condition.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 3.05 provides that no person shall be denied initial licensure or renewal due to any complaint, criminal charge, conviction, judgment, discipline or other sanction arising from providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive or gender-affirming health care services, so long as the services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice here. Both qualifiers are satisfied on these facts.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation removes this category of sanction as a basis for denial.
choice_analysis.B: The protection does not depend on the other state vacating its action.
choice_analysis.C: Deferring renewal pending investigation of the protected conduct would defeat the protection.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the sanction may not be used as a basis for denial.
choice_analysis.E: Attaching probation on that basis would be denial in substance.

related_facts: Parallel protections apply to pharmacy support personnel under 247 CMR 8.08 and to pharmacies under 247 CMR 6.18.
explanation.mpje_trap: The protection is conditional on the two qualifiers, but once they are met the sanction cannot be recycled as a denial basis.

reasoning_steps: Identify the sanction as arising solely from protected health care activity
Test the lawful-in-Massachusetts and good-practice qualifiers
Apply the bar on using that sanction as a basis for denial
